_comment: EXT-63, arm 30 — 3 h, LV-1 + LV-2 ONLY (no LV-4, no LV-5).  The 43 %-admission
posture, taken past one hour for the first time.
WHY THIS ARM EXISTS.  The §13.5 over-retention audit (run 2026-08-05 on the arms
already on disk, same build Aug 4 2026 23:27:25) attributes the DATA-side cost of the
LV ladder to LV-4 and to LV-4 ALONE.  On IDENTICAL observation counts (87936 phase obs,
61 stations, settled 20-60 min):
arm                    LV-4  demean  LV-1   postfit phase rms   settled a00
canonical               -      -      -         0.01020 m          17.45
LV-4 alone             YES     -      -         0.01670 m           2.69
Every arm carrying LV-4 sits at 0.0166-0.0167; every arm without it at 0.0100-0.0102.
The de-mean and the seed frame move the LEVEL by ~33 TECU and cost NOTHING on the data
side; LV-4 costs +64 % postfit phase rms and moves the level DOWN ~15 TECU.  The same
split holds at 12 h (canonical 0.01130 m vs full stack 0.01580 m, +40 %, and +44 % in
the settled h6-12 window) and the prior side agrees (prires rxcb sigma0 1.92 -> 12.62).
So SPEC §15.2's 'LV-4 makes the carry's information admissible at all — keep' is
contradicted by the audit it asked for.  The retired frame-dependent screen withheld
67 % of the carry folds; its STATISTIC was frame-dependent (that critique stands), but
the folds it withheld are ones the observations do not support.  Accidental budget,
one level below where §11.3 found it.
This arm therefore keeps the two knobs that set the LEVEL (LV-1 seed frame, LV-2
common-mode de-mean) and drops the one that costs the DATA fit.  LV-5 is off because
it is nearly inert without LV-4 (§12) and because the lag-1 loop is measured STABLE at
this admission fraction — §11.3: 'stable at 33 %, oscillating at 97.5 %', and arm 19
measured settled sd 4.98 at 1 h.
PREDICTION, STATED BEFORE THE RUN.
1. LEVEL tracks the full stack within about +-3 TECU, i.e. it RAMPS the same way.
Reasoning: once the de-mean is on, admission barely moves the level (1 h settled
37.43 at 43 % vs 35.24 at 97.5 %, only 2.2 TECU apart) because the de-mean is what
removes the common-mode force in the first place.  Against the time-matched GIM
that predicts roughly +7 at hour 2 and +15 at hour 3 (stack was +4.9 / +13.2).
If it ramps LESS, LV-4 was feeding the ramp and that is a new result.
2. DATA side stays at the canonical's level: median postfit phase rms 0.009-0.010 m
in hours 2-3, NOT the stack's 0.0130 m.  This is the claim the arm exists to test —
the stack's level without the stack's residual penalty.
3. prires rxcb sigma0 stays near the canonical's ~1.0 (h2-3), not the stack's 8.4.
4. rx-CB carry folds ~43 % of harvests (the retired screen is back in force), erases 0
(no LV-4 step gate exists in this arm).
GRADE (CLAUDE.md amendment 6): scripts/gim_global_mean_series.py AND
scripts/field_vs_gim_footprint.py, both time-matched.  NEVER against the single number
'GIM 32.24'.  Hours 0-1 are ignition (§14: the level channel's budget is ~2 h) and are
reported as such; hours 2-3 are the legal read.  3 h CANNOT settle the long-horizon
walk that separated the postures only from hour ~5 (§15) — that stays open.
DENOMINATOR: runs/ext63_dual_12h_ref hours 0-3, same build, same window, same lineage.
No new canonical run is needed — a forward-only filter's hours 0-3 do not depend on
max_duration_s.
FRESH LINEAGE ONLY: LV-1 and LV-2 are fingerprinted.  Own paths; never resume.
